comments.value: Here is a picture of the new UI/UX for reference

This is mostly perhaps a bug than a feature but still, the icons to the left of the upper menu bar is not a good placement or to have it tied to the clock. 

Again, notifications, security, these are things that should be at the bottom along with the rest of the menu functions. This is what I am talking about with a busy menu as you would have to scan all over to find the features for the functions that you need. I won't restate all that I had above but I hope that it illustrates the issues with the new UI/UX.
Security Settings is still one of the big main buttons on the Quick Menu which is probably why it's relegated to being a small button on the main menu, as that's the secondary location.

details:
I go by the motto, if it isn't broken, don't fix it.

For who is on your UI/UX team who decided it was a good idea to change the UI and the UX (User Interface and User Experience) needs to have their position re-evaluated and the one who approved it out of beta and pushed to stable with out rigorous testing also needs to have their position re-evaluated. 

The issues are as follows. The Icons for the Security and Notifications has been pushed to the top of the menu and placed on the same bar as the clock. When the clock is changed in it's appearance, it also changes the size of this bar and its icons to reflect the size of the clock, this is a horrible idea. If you want a smaller clock, it will make the buttons smaller. 

The most important feature is the security settings. Whether you are bouncing from a private world, to a public one, or is facing major lag in a club world, or the potential of unoptimized and crashers, the most used feature outside of your social, worlds, and avatars is the safety settings. Placing this in a hard to reach area of the UI, makes the UX that much more horrible for the user. Again, if it isn't broken, don't fix it.

Oversized UI Canvas. The Canvas which the UI is displayed on when the menu is opened. is oversized. The size also changes dependant on which sub menu is opened, IE social, groups, avatars, etc. This is horrible on VR mode where one has to constantly push and pull away the menu from one self in order to properly read the menu. This is also bad equally on desktop where the menu padding from the boarders are nearly meeting the edge of the screen and on other odd ratio monitors, this creates menu clipping. Again, if it isn't broken DON'T FIX IT.

The menu is too busy and clustered. The additional icons and space being split makes it hard to navigate and confusing to any normal user, and with a huge majority being on quest, which the demographic analytics should reflect, is entry level users with little technical skills, the UI/UX is too clustered in many areas and busy in others which has one moving all around the entire canvas space just to access the features that should be easy to access. Having features which are behind a single click is better than having all the features displayed on the menu all at once, this is why every Microsoft program since the dawn of 3.5, had their file systems displayed with roll out menus. File, Edit, etc. This creates ease of access where like features are easily accessible under a like roll out and keeps the main display from being clustered. All menus are also in the same area, where at the top, they all are easily accessed. For VR chat however, everything has always been at the bottom of the canvas space and so why then would certain menu's be then moved to the top while others are on the bottom? This breaks the UI and confusing for the UX. 

I hope that your development team reconsiders the decisions for the new update and I hope that the menu would be reverted back to the original design to where improvements to that layout will be considered instead of trying to fix what isn't broken.

I come from a background of interactive software development and have been in the field since 2004. I hope that my words don't land on deaf ears. 

Thank you. Red.
title: UI/UX
